title: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Kings 23](/bible/2-kings/23)

This session covers [2 Kings 23](/bible/2-kings/23) through 25. It follows Josiah as he hears the book of the law that was found in the house of the Most High, rends his clothes in the fear of the Lord, and leads the whole nation in a covenant to keep the commandments. He tears down the idols, altars, and high places that his fathers had set up, keeps a great Passover, and turns to the Lord with all his heart. Yet the wrath kindled by Manasseh's sins is not turned away: Josiah is slain at Megiddo, his sons do evil, and the reading moves through the fall of Judah, the burning of the temple, and the carrying away of the people to Babylon, closing with a note of mercy shown to Jehoiachin. The thread throughout is repentance: seeing in the book of the law why the nation is in its condition and turning back to keep what is written.

**[2 Kings 23:1-3](/bible/2-kings/23#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-kings/23#v1)</sup> And the king sent, and they gathered unto him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-kings/23#v2)</sup> And the king went up into the house of the Lord, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people, both small and great: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-kings/23#v3)</sup> And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

- Josiah gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, went up to the house of the Most High with the priests, the prophets, and all the people both small and great, and read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found there.
- Our forefathers had the Bible; the king read it openly, then stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the Lord to walk after him and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all their heart and soul.
- All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book.
  - **[2 Kings 22:8](/bible/2-kings/22#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/2-kings/22#v8)</sup> And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

    Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law in the house of the Lord and gave it to Shaphan the scribe, who read it.
  - **[2 Kings 22:13](/bible/2-kings/22#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/2-kings/22#v13)</sup> Go ye, enquire of the Lord for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found: for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book, to do according unto all that which is written concerning us.

    Josiah sent to inquire of the Lord because great was the wrath kindled against them, for the fathers had not hearkened to the words of this book.
  - **[2 Kings 22:16-17](/bible/2-kings/22#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/2-kings/22#v16)</sup> Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants thereof, even all the words of the book which the king of Judah hath read:
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/2-kings/22#v17)</sup> Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense unto other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the works of their hands; therefore my wrath shall be kindled against this place, and shall not be quenched.

    The Lord answered that he would bring evil on the place because they forsook him and burnt incense to other gods, and his wrath would not be quenched.

**[2 Kings 23:4-5](/bible/2-kings/23#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/2-kings/23#v4)</sup> And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Beth–el.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-kings/23#v5)</sup> And he put down the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places round about Jerusalem; them also that burned incense unto Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of heaven.

- The king commanded Hilkiah and the priests to bring out of the temple all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all the host of heaven, and he burned them in the fields of Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.
- He put down the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places and around Jerusalem, and those that burnt incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the planets, and all the host of heaven.
- When Josiah read the law the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong.
  - **[Deuteronomy 7:25-26](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v25)**
    > <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v25)</sup> The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v26)</sup> Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.

    The graven images of their gods are to be burned with fire, and their silver and gold not desired, for it is a cursed and abominable thing to bring into the house.
  - **[Deuteronomy 4:19](/bible/deuteronomy/4#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/4#v19)</sup> And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which the Lord thy God hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.

    Israel was not to lift up their eyes and be driven to worship the sun, moon, and stars, which the Lord divided to the other nations.

**[2 Kings 23:6-9](/bible/2-kings/23#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/2-kings/23#v6)</sup> And he brought out the grove from the house of the Lord, without Jerusalem, unto the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder, and cast the powder thereof upon the graves of the children of the people.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-kings/23#v7)</sup> And he brake down the houses of the sodomites, that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-kings/23#v8)</sup> And he brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beer–sheba, and brake down the high places of the gates that were in the entering in of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man’s left hand at the gate of the city.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-kings/23#v9)</sup> Nevertheless the priests of the high places came not up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, but they did eat of the unleavened bread among their brethren.

- He brought the grove out of the house of the Lord to the brook Kidron, burned it, stamped it to powder, and cast the powder on the graves of the children of the people.
- He broke down the houses of the sodomites that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove; there should be no sodomite among the sons of Israel, yet they had grown so bold as to do this wickedness right beside the temple.
- He brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where they had burnt incense, and though the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar, they still ate of the unleavened bread among their brethren.

**[2 Kings 23:10](/bible/2-kings/23#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/2-kings/23#v10)</sup> And he defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

- Josiah defiled Topheth in the valley of the children of Hinnom so that no man might make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.
- Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own.
  - **[Jeremiah 1:1-3](/bible/jeremiah/1#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/jeremiah/1#v1)</sup> The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin:
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/jeremiah/1#v2)</sup> To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/jeremiah/1#v3)</sup> It came also in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, unto the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah the son of Josiah king of Judah, unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.

    Jeremiah son of Hilkiah prophesied in the days of Josiah through Zedekiah, showing he was a prophet during this very time of reform.
  - **[Jeremiah 7:31-33](/bible/jeremiah/7#v31)**
    > <sup>[31](/bible/jeremiah/7#v31)</sup> And they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.
    >
    > <sup>[32](/bible/jeremiah/7#v32)</sup> Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place.
    >
    > <sup>[33](/bible/jeremiah/7#v33)</sup> And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and none shall fray them away.

    Because they built the high places of Topheth to burn their sons and daughters, the Lord said it would be called the valley of slaughter and their carcases would be meat for the fowls.

**[2 Kings 23:11-14](/bible/2-kings/23#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/2-kings/23#v11)</sup> And he took away the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entering in of the house of the Lord, by the chamber of Nathan–melech the chamberlain, which was in the suburbs, and burned the chariots of the sun with fire.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-kings/23#v12)</sup> And the altars that were on the top of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, did the king beat down, and brake them down from thence, and cast the dust of them into the brook Kidron.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-kings/23#v13)</sup> And the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mount of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had builded for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon, did the king defile.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-kings/23#v14)</sup> And he brake in pieces the images, and cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men.

- He took away the horses the kings of Judah had given to the sun and burnt the chariots of the sun with fire.
- He beat down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's chamber and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron.
- He defiled the high places Solomon had built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom, the abominations of the Zidonians, Moabites, and Ammonites, and broke in pieces the images, cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men.
- This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and to fall under punishment.
  - **[1 Kings 11:5-7](/bible/1-kings/11#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/1-kings/11#v5)</sup> For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/1-kings/11#v6)</sup> And Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and went not fully after the Lord, as did David his father.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/1-kings/11#v7)</sup> Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.

    In his old age Solomon went after Ashtoreth, Milcom, and Chemosh and built high places for these abominations, the corruption Josiah now tore down.

**[2 Kings 23:15-18](/bible/2-kings/23#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/2-kings/23#v15)</sup> Moreover the altar that was at Beth–el, and the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, had made, both that altar and the high place he brake down, and burned the high place, and stamped it small to powder, and burned the grove.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-kings/23#v16)</sup> And as Josiah turned himself, he spied the sepulchres that were there in the mount, and sent, and took the bones out of the sepulchres, and burned them upon the altar, and polluted it, according to the word of the Lord which the man of God proclaimed, who proclaimed these words.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-kings/23#v17)</sup> Then he said, What title is that that I see? And the men of the city told him, It is the sepulchre of the man of God, which came from Judah, and proclaimed these things that thou hast done against the altar of Beth–el.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-kings/23#v18)</sup> And he said, Let him alone; let no man move his bones. So they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet that came out of Samaria.

- Josiah also destroyed the altar and high place at Bethel that Jeroboam had made when he set up the golden calves, burning it and stamping it small to powder.
- Turning himself, he spied the sepulchres in the mount, took out the bones, and burnt them upon the altar to pollute it, according to the word the man of God had proclaimed.
- When told which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who prophesied these things, he said to let him alone and let no man move his bones.
  - **[1 Kings 13:2](/bible/1-kings/13#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/13#v2)</sup> And he cried against the altar in the word of the Lord, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the Lord; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.

    The man of God cried against the altar of Bethel that a child named Josiah would be born to David's house and offer the priests of the high places upon it, and burn men's bones on it.

**[2 Kings 23:19-20](/bible/2-kings/23#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/2-kings/23#v19)</sup> And all the houses also of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, Josiah took away, and did to them according to all the acts that he had done in Beth–el.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-kings/23#v20)</sup> And he slew all the priests of the high places that were there upon the altars, and burned men’s bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.

- Josiah also took away all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, and did to them as he had done at Bethel.
- The northern kingdom had already been carried into captivity by Assyria, so most of the people were gone, yet the idolatrous houses remained.
- He slew all the priests of the high places upon their altars, burnt men's bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.

**[2 Kings 23:21-23](/bible/2-kings/23#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/2-kings/23#v21)</sup> And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the passover unto the Lord your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-kings/23#v22)</sup> Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah;
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-kings/23#v23)</sup> But in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, wherein this passover was holden to the Lord in Jerusalem.

- The king commanded all the people to keep the Passover to the Lord their God as it is written in the book of this covenant.
- Such a Passover had not been held from the days of the judges nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah, but in the eighteenth year of Josiah this Passover was held in Jerusalem.
- Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today.
  - **[1 Esdras 1:1](/bible/1-esdras/1#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/1-esdras/1#v1)</sup> And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem unto his Lord, and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month;

    Josiah held the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
  - **[1 Esdras 1:9](/bible/1-esdras/1#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/1-esdras/1#v9)</sup> And Jeconias, and Samaias, and Nathanael his brother, and Assabias, and Ochiel, and Joram, captains over thousands, gave to the Levites for the passover five thousand sheep, and seven hundred calves.

    The magnitude of the offering showed how great and well ordered this Passover was.

**[2 Kings 23:24-27](/bible/2-kings/23#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/2-kings/23#v24)</sup> Moreover the workers with familiar spirits, and the wizards, and the images, and the idols, and all the abominations that were spied in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, did Josiah put away, that he might perform the words of the law which were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-kings/23#v25)</sup> And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/2-kings/23#v26)</sup> Notwithstanding the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-kings/23#v27)</sup> And the Lord said, I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.

- Josiah also put away the workers with familiar spirits, the wizards, the images, the idols, and all the abominations spied in Judah and Jerusalem, that he might perform the words of the law found by Hilkiah.
- There was no king before or after him that turned to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might according to all the law of Moses; he put things in order like a true leader.
- Nevertheless the Lord did not turn from the fierceness of his great wrath because of the provocations of Manasseh, and said he would remove Judah out of his sight as he had removed Israel and cast off Jerusalem.

**[2 Kings 23:28-30](/bible/2-kings/23#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/2-kings/23#v28)</sup> Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/2-kings/23#v29)</sup> In his days Pharaoh–nechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates: and king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo, when he had seen him.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/2-kings/23#v30)</sup> And his servants carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own sepulchre. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father’s stead.

- Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates, and Josiah went against him and was slain at Megiddo.
- Josiah got involved in a matter that did not concern him and lost his life in it, a warning not to enter into quarrels that are not one's own.
- His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem and buried him, and the people took Jehoahaz his son and anointed him king in his father's place.

**[2 Kings 23:31-37](/bible/2-kings/23#v31)**

> <sup>[31](/bible/2-kings/23#v31)</sup> Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/2-kings/23#v32)</sup> And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/2-kings/23#v33)</sup> And Pharaoh–nechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and put the land to a tribute of an hundred talents of silver, and a talent of gold.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/2-kings/23#v34)</sup> And Pharaoh–nechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz away: and he came to Egypt, and died there.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/2-kings/23#v35)</sup> And Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; but he taxed the land to give the money according to the commandment of Pharaoh: he exacted the silver and the gold of the people of the land, of every one according to his taxation, to give it unto Pharaoh–nechoh.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/2-kings/23#v36)</sup> Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/2-kings/23#v37)</sup> And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.

- Jehoahaz was twenty three years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done.
- Pharaohnechoh bound him at Riblah so he might not reign, put the land to a tribute of silver and gold, and made Eliakim the son of Josiah king, turning his name to Jehoiakim.
- Jehoiakim taxed the people to pay Pharaoh, exacting the silver and gold of every man of the land, and he also did evil in the sight of the Lord like his forefathers, not like his father Josiah.
